data.name: Demetri
data.gender_notes: Demetri is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name ‘Demetrios’, meaning ‘follower of Demeter’. Demeter is the Greek goddess of agriculture, harvest, and fertility. The name Demetri honors her and represents the bountiful fruits of the earth and the sustenance of life. The name Demetri carries the meaning “Follower of Demeter” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Demetri usually hope their child will grow to embody follower of demeter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of abundance, prosperity, and nurturing relationships.
data.etymology: Demetri belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Follower of Demeter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Demetri total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
data.cultural_impact: The name Demetri has historical significance as it is associated with a renowned early Christian saint, Saint Demetrius of Thessalonica. He is best known for miraculous protection during military battles and for intercession in matters related to health and fertility. The name continues to be popular in Eastern Christianity, particularly in Eastern Europe, as a symbol of courage, strength, and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: Demetri, as a Christian name derived from a Greek goddess, reflects the divine intersection between various spiritual traditions. It serves as a reminder of the unity of all creation and the inherent spiritual power found within our natural world. It also highlights the transformative nature of faith, as humans have turned from the worship of Demeter to following the teachings of Christ while maintaining some connection to earlier traditions.
